title: I tow abandoned cars at night. The one on my hook keeps flashing its lights.
story:
The headlights behind me flashed twice, bright enough to light up my whole cab. The car on my hook was empty. I'd checked.

Dispatch sent me out at one in the morning to a gray sedan on the shoulder of a county road. Keys in the ignition. Nobody around. The only strange thing was the windows, fogged up thick, like someone had been sitting inside breathing for hours.

I hooked it, lifted it, and pulled out. Two miles later, the horn started. One long blast. Then the lights again.

I pulled over and walked back with my flashlight. Doors locked. Seats empty. But on the fogged back window, there was a fresh handprint, pressed from the inside.

So I called dispatch. She was quiet for a second. "The owner just phoned," she said. "He says he's still with his car. He says you took him."

I didn't answer. I was staring at the handprint. It was slowly fading as the glass cleared. Like whoever made it had just climbed out.

I ran back to my truck and locked the doors. The engine was running. The heater was on. And the passenger window right beside me was starting to fog up.

From the inside.
premise: night tow driver hauls an empty fogged-up sedan; the owner says he's still with his car; the fog appears on the tow truck's own passenger window
